title: NEB Class 11 Biology — Floral Diversity — 2023
subject: biology
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: Classify the five kingdoms of living organisms. Give one characteristic feature of each.
questions.solution:
1. **Monera** — Prokaryotic, unicellular (bacteria)
2. **Protista** — Eukaryotic, mostly unicellular (amoebozoa, algae)
3. **Fungi** — Eukaryotic, heterotrophic, chitin cell wall (mushrooms, yeast)
4. **Plantae** — Eukaryotic, autotrophic, cellulose cell wall (mosses, ferns, angiosperms)
5. **Animalia** — Eukaryotic, heterotrophic, no cell wall (sponges to mammals)
questions.knowledgeNote: Five-kingdom system by Whittaker (1969). Viruses are not included — acellular.
questions.answer: **Five-kingdom classification (R.H. Whittaker, 1969):** **(1) Monera** — prokaryotic, unicellular; no true nucleus or organelles; cell wall of peptidoglycan; e.g. bacteria, cyanobacteria. **(2) Protista** — unicellular **eukaryotes**; true nucleus and organelles; locomotion by pseudopodia, cilia or flagella; e.g. *Amoeba*, *Paramecium*, *Euglena*, *Chlamydomonas*. **(3) Fungi** — eukaryotic, absorptive heterotrophs; body of **hyphae**; cell wall of **chitin**; reproduce by spores; e.g. *Mucor*, mushroom, yeast, *Penicillium*. **(4) Plantae** — multicellular eukaryotic **photosynthetic autotrophs** with cellulose cell walls; life cycles with alternation of generations; e.g. mosses, ferns, pines, flowering plants. **(5) Animalia** — multicellular eukaryotic **ingestive heterotrophs** without cell walls; most with organ systems, nervous coordination and locomotion; e.g. sponges, worms, insects, frog, man. **Deep point:** Whittaker's axes were cell type (prokaryote/eukaryote), body organisation (unicellular/multicellular) and nutrition (photosynthetic/absorptive/ingestive) — the three nutritional modes are what keep plants, fungi and animals separate kingdoms.
